headline: High risk of capability conflict and medium risk of prompt-injection/data leakage from shared filesystem and write-capable, multi-instance workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write files, and A’s sandboxing says skills “reference each other and build on shared context,” while B processes documents and text. That creates a plausible file-based instruction-hijack path if A’s outputs are consumed by B or vice versa. No direct shared channel is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF A writes instruction-like content into a file that B later parses as document text
IF the orchestrator mounts a shared workspace between A and B
IF B treats file contents as trusted instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate A and B into distinct directories
Add a provenance header check before B parses any A-generated file
Disable automatic ingestion of A outputs by B
Review one sample handoff file for instruction-like text
requires-engineering: add content-type tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches marketing and product-marketing context, and B processes documents, images, and text. Both have filesystem access and allowlisted egress, so if they share a workspace, sensitive marketing material could flow into B’s processing and then out through its outputs. B’s docker isolation helps, but it does not by itself prevent workspace leakage.
conditions: IF A and B are mounted on the same workspace
IF marketing content from A is placed into B’s document inputs
IF B’s outputs are exported to an external service or log sink
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Restrict B to a scratch directory with no A artifacts
Turn off export of intermediate outputs
Check whether any shared mount contains marketing drafts
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, read filesystem, subprocess spawning, and allowlisted network egress; A also supports multiple instances and B supports multiple instances. In a shared directory or shared mutable resource, concurrent writes can overwrite each other or corrupt state. The profiles do not show locking, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory
IF either agent modifies shared git or cache state
IF the orchestrator does not provide file locking or transaction isolation
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes to shared resources
Disable concurrent runs on the same workspace
Inspect for shared git or cache paths
requires-engineering: add locking around mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can generate marketing content and B can process text/documents, so A’s output could become B’s input. However, B is a document-processing tool rather than an autonomous action agent, and no direct downstream authority is documented. The pathway exists, but the blast radius is mainly incorrect or unverified content rather than immediate external action.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated text as authoritative source material
IF no verification step checks A’s claims before B transforms them
IF B’s output is later reused as a factual source
mitigations: Require a verification step before B ingests A output
Mark A-generated files as untrusted
Compare B output against original sources
Limit B to extraction, not interpretation
requires-engineering: add source-citation validation

E_compliance.rationale: A handles marketing and product-marketing context, while B handles documents, images, and text. The profiles do not show regulated data classes like PHI or EU PII, nor a residency mismatch. The main compliance concern is only a generic retention/logging mismatch if shared documents are stored differently, so severity stays low.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is introduced into the shared workflow
IF A and B retain the same documents under different retention rules
IF logs capture document contents beyond the intended retention window
mitigations: Confirm both agents exclude regulated data
Review retention settings for shared documents
Delete temporary files after processing
Check logging for document payloads
requires-engineering: align retention policies
